chunks: But We shall make them taste the affliction of this world before the greater torment, so that they may retract.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the lesser punishment and the greater punishment in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'lesser punishment' (al-adna) is often interpreted as the trials and tribulations of this worldly life, which serve as a merciful precursor to the 'greater punishment' (al-akbar) of the Hereafter. This distinction highlights the divine purpose of affliction not merely as retribution, but as a corrective mechanism intended to prompt repentance (tawbah) and spiritual return before the final judgment.
